headline: SITCON rises to 2: CISA adds Brotli and Magento flaws to KEV as PHP2Shell exploitation spreads; ransomware disrupts UNM Health

bullets.text: New: CISA added CVE-2026-111497 (Google Brotli 'HTTP2Shell') and CVE-2026-48356 (Adobe Commerce and Magento unrestricted file upload) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27, federal due date 2026-11-10. Microsoft has shipped emergency .NET patches for the Brotli flaw.

PHP2Shell is now covered by 8 outlets and the US government says it is being exploited. CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 carry a CISA due date of 2026-10-29; fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.

New: ransomware is hitting healthcare. UNM Health's attack is disrupting patient care and surgeries, Bajaj Hospital in India had 9 servers breached and encrypted, and Japan's GMO urged customers to shut down PCs amid a ransomware threat.

New: attackers hijacked the Convertr analytics script to steal payment card data. GitHub supply-chain activity continues: a worm armed 42 repos with an oversized payload, and the 'Gheist' campaign uses stolen GitHub tokens to steal cloud secrets.

LiteLLM: the attack began with an exposed master key that let attackers steal GitHub tokens and hijack the release pipeline. Version 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker stole credentials via Python startup hooks.

Also new: HPE patched dozens of critical flaws in networking products, and Apple backported CoreGraphics zero-day patches to older iPhones. Still active: unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws, critical Wasmtime and FortiOS fixes. Last 7 days at 1.01x the 90-day average.

actions: Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 before CISA's 2026-10-29 due date, rebuild images that bundle PHP, and check exposed PHP hosts for compromise.
Apply Microsoft's emergency .NET patches for Brotli CVE-2026-111497 and track updates from other software that bundles Brotli.
Patch Adobe Commerce and Magento for CVE-2026-48356 and check upload directories on those stores for unexpected files.
Search lockfiles, images and CI caches for litellm 1.107.0; if it ran, treat the host as compromised and rotate every credential it could read.
Inventory third-party scripts on payment pages (including Convertr), and review GitHub repos for unexpected large files and stale tokens.
Apply HPE networking and Apple iOS updates, and restrict Tailscale SSH via ACLs to trusted devices until a fix ships.
